author: Gerard Manley Hopkins
title: Poems of Gerard Manley Hopkins, now first published
edition: Edited by Robert Bridges; London: Humphrey Milford, 1918. Wikisource transcription of the 1918 scan (Index:Poems of Gerard Manley Hopkins, 1918.djvu, from Internet Archive poemsofgerardman030114mbp), read against the page images line by line. It replaces Project Gutenberg 22403, the earlier source of this text, which dropped Hopkins's stress marks or spelled them out (faawn-froth for fáwn-fróth, houers for hoürs). The text now carries every acute, grave (as in -èd) and diaeresis mark the book prints, including eleven the Wikisource transcription itself lacks (mércy, wé, aftèr, únselve, deárly, áre, ís, Cán, Í, wóodlark, thínk) and one it misplaces (quíte for qúite); the accent the book sets over the n of Ońe in The Golden Echo is kept there. Where the print, the transcription and Gutenberg disagree in words or punctuation, the print is followed. The library text holds Hopkins's own Author's Preface and every poem and fragment (Early Poems, Poems 1876-1889, Unfinished Poems & Fragments, nos. 1-74, with 73 and 74, which Gutenberg left out); the title page, Bridges's dedicatory sonnet, the Editor's Preface to Notes and Notes, the facsimile and its reference under poem 67 are omitted. Conventions: poem numbers and titles are level-3 headings without italics, the book's section titles level-2 headings; verse keeps the printed lines and stanzas, each turned-over line as an indented continuation line; italics are underscore emphasis, dashes double hyphens, small-capital opening words capitals, the book's rows of dots indented dotted lines; Hopkins's division bar is |, and the pause and twirl signs the Preface explains are 𝄐 and ~; the stanza numbers of The Wreck of the Deutschland and other numbered poems open their stanzas, and poems 30 and 37 keep their printed line numbers. Bridges's two editorial footnotes inside the Author's Preface are kept: each call becomes [*] and each note a paragraph [Footnote *: text] right after the paragraph that calls it.

rights.basis: The English text in this 1918 London edition was published before 1931; its US publication copyright term has expired as of 2026. The Wikimedia Commons scan the transcription is made from is tagged PD-US. No later editorial introduction is included.

The wikitext was reduced to running text (Page: headers, footers, running heads, page-quality markup, HTML comments and templates removed, small capitals and gaps marked) and compared word by word with the Project Gutenberg 22403 library text it replaces (380 blocks; their block division, indentation, continuation lines and dotted lines are kept). The transcription's marked words were carried into that text, and every marked word and every difference in words, punctuation, lines or stanzas was decided on the page images (Wikimedia Commons renderings of the djvu and the Internet Archive scan). From the earlier text: 80 of its blocks gain stress marks (242 marked words); words corrected where Gutenberg misread the print (hawling, wild-worst, perishing, thee, gulf's, fáwn, hoürs, greenworld, plumèd, cheevo, and an O restored in Spelt from Sibyl's Leaves, The Blessed Virgin compared to the Air we Breathe and St. Winefred's Well); punctuation restored in the Preface (outrides, and two dashes), The Wreck of the Deutschland, Penmaen Pool, Spring, The Loss of the Eurydice, The Bugler's First Communion, Brothers, The Leaden Echo and the Golden Echo, The Blessed Virgin, To what serves Mortal Beauty? and St. Winefred's Well; the Preface's line-end hyphens super-inducing and counter-point closed up, mounting italic, its equation's last term printed as = 10½, and the pause and twirl signs restored; headings 15 The Caged Skylark, 42 Tom's Garland: upon the Unemployed and 58 St. Winefred's Well (Gutenberg: Caged Skylark; Tom's Garland; 53); one continuation line in poem 53 indented as printed. The Leaden Echo, which Gutenberg split after 'from vanishing away?', is one stanza as printed, so the earlier block 247 now ends block 246 and blocks 248 onward move up one. Poems 73 and 74 (printed pages 91-92) were added at the end as level-3 headings with their stanzas. The margin line numbers that the first conversion had left at the ends of verse lines (in Brothers and The Blessed Virgin compared to the Air we Breathe) were taken out on 2026-11-18.
